metadata.documentation: Therapeutic substances and pharmacological agents acting directly or indirectly on the heart and circulatory vascular system to treat cardiovascular disorders.
Drugs used in the prophylaxis and management of acute or chronic arterial hypertension to prevent vascular complications such as stroke and myocardial infarction.
Competitive antagonists of beta-adrenergic receptors that attenuate the chronotropic and inotropic effects of catecholamines on myocardial and vascular tissue.
Inhibitors of angiotensin-converting enzyme that decrease circulating angiotensin II and aldosterone concentrations, promoting vasodilation and natriuresis.
Selective antagonists of the angiotensin II type 1 (AT1) receptor that inhibit vasoconstrictor and aldosterone-secreting actions of angiotensin II.
Agents that inhibit the transmembrane influx of calcium ions through voltage-gated L-type calcium channels in cardiac muscle and vascular smooth muscle.
Agents used to prevent or suppress cardiac arrhythmias by altering electrophysiological properties of the myocardium and conducting system.
Therapeutic substances utilized to normalize aberrant plasma lipid and lipoprotein profiles, targeting reduction of atherogenic cholesterol fractions.
Competitive inhibitors of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme in hepatic cholesterol biosynthesis.
Monoclonal antibodies or small interfering RNAs targeting proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 to enhance hepatic LDL-receptor recycling.
Agents that prevent or delay the clotting of blood by impairing the synthesis or activity of coagulation factors.
Orally active small-molecule inhibitors directly targeting activated Factor X (FXa) or thrombin (Factor IIa) in the coagulation cascade.
Compounds that suppress platelet activation, adhesion, or aggregation to inhibit intravascular thrombus formation.
Substances that promote the excretion of water and electrolytes, primarily sodium, through the kidneys to reduce intravascular volume.
Potent natriuretic diuretics that act primarily by inhibiting the Na+/K+/2Cl- cotransporter in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle.
Diuretic agents that inhibit NaCl cotransport in the distal convoluted tubule of the nephron, moderating blood pressure and fluid retention.
Agents modifying neuronal neurotransmission, synaptic signaling, or cellular excitability within the brain and spinal cord.
Therapeutic substances used in the alleviation of affective disorders, major depressive episodes, dysthymia, and related mood conditions.
Compounds selectively blocking the neuronal presynaptic serotonin transporter protein (SERT), potentiating serotonergic neurotransmission.
Dual reuptake inhibitors that block both serotonin and norepinephrine transporters, utilized in major depression, generalized anxiety, and neuropathic pain.
Psychopharmacological agents prescribed in schizophrenia, bipolar mania, and psychotic disorders to mitigate delusions, hallucinations, and thought disorganization.
Antipsychotics characterized by dual dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptor antagonism with lower risk of acute extrapyramidal symptoms.
Diverse class of pharmacological agents that reduce excessive neuronal hyperexcitability and suppress seizure propagation across epileptic networks.
Antiepileptic molecules that stabilize the inactive conformation of voltage-dependent neuronal sodium channels to limit sustained high-frequency action potential firing.
Therapeutic substances utilized for sedation, anxiolysis, induction of sleep, and alleviation of acute psychomotor agitation.
Positive allosteric modulators of the GABAA receptor that enhance chloride conductance, yielding anxiolytic, sedative, anticonvulsant, and muscle-relaxant actions.
Compounds designed to relieve acute or chronic pain without inducing total anesthesia or loss of consciousness.
Agonists targeting central and peripheral mu-, kappa-, and delta-opioid receptors to modulate ascending pain pathways and nociceptive thresholds.
Broad therapeutic umbrella comprising pharmaceutical agents that eradicate or inhibit the proliferation of pathogenic microorganisms.
Substances of natural, semi-synthetic, or synthetic origin that destroy bacterial organisms or inhibit their cellular growth and replication.
Beta-lactam antibiotics that covalently bind penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), disrupting peptidoglycan cell-wall cross-linking and triggering autolysis.
Class of beta-lactam bactericidal antibiotics derived from Acremonium, categorized across five generations of antimicrobial spectrum and beta-lactamase stability.
Synthetic bactericidal antimicrobials that inhibit bacterial DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV, preventing replication and transcription.
Bacteriostatic antibiotics characterized by a large macrocyclic lactone ring that bind reversibly to the 50S ribosomal subunit to impede protein elongation.
Substances used in managing viral infections by inhibiting specific phases of the viral life cycle, including cellular entry, uncoating, replication, and egress.
Purine or pyrimidine nucleoside analogues that act as chain terminators during retroviral viral reverse transcription of RNA into proviral DNA.
Medicinal preparations designed to eradicate or prevent fungal infections by targeting fungal cell membranes, ergosterol synthesis, or cell wall beta-glucan polymers.
Synthetic azole compounds containing a five-membered diunsaturated ring with three nitrogen atoms, inhibiting lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase (CYP51).
Substances used to treat malignant neoplasms or modulate host immune responsiveness, including cytostatics, targeted kinase inhibitors, and biologics.
Engineered immunoglobulins targeting tumor-specific antigens to trigger antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity, complement activation, or signaling pathway interruption.
Immunotherapeutic antibodies that disinhibit cytotoxic T cells by blocking regulatory co-inhibitory receptors such as PD-1, PD-L1, or CTLA-4.
Small-molecule pharmaceuticals that competitively block ATP-binding catalytic domains of receptor or non-receptor tyrosine kinases involved in oncogenic signaling.
Pharmaceutical compounds indicated to restore glycemic control and reduce microvascular and macrovascular complications in patients with diabetes mellitus.
Incretin mimetics that bind the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor, augmenting glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppressing glucagon, and slowing gastric emptying.
Oral hypoglycemic agents that inhibit renal SGLT2 in the proximal convoluted tubule, inducing glucosuria and osmotic diuresis.
Secretagogue oral antidiabetic agents that bind the SUR1 subunit of ATP-sensitive potassium channels in pancreatic beta cells, triggering endogenous insulin release.
Pharmacological preparations utilized to treat pathology of the gastrointestinal tract, including acid secretion disorders, motility dysfunction, and inflammatory states.
Substituted benzimidazoles that irreversibly inhibit the H+/K+-ATPase enzyme system in gastric parietal cells, blocking terminal hydrochloric acid secretion.
Medicinal agents acting upon the lungs and airways to manage obstructive, restrictive, or inflammatory pulmonary diseases.
Topically delivered glucocorticoid receptor agonists that suppress airway inflammation, reduce mucosal edema, and decrease bronchial hyperresponsiveness.
